mount.title: Mount {{name}} on your device
mount.lede: Use this address as a network drive.
mount.step.mac: Finder opens the files as a read-only drive.
mount.mac.1: In Finder, choose Go > Connect to Server (Command-K).
mount.mac.2: Paste the address in the Server Address field.
mount.mac.4: Open the drive under Locations in the Finder sidebar.
mount.step.windows: File Explorer opens the files as a drive with its own letter.
mount.windows.1: Open File Explorer and select This PC.
mount.windows.2: Select More (the … button), then Map network drive.
mount.windows.2.note: Windows 10: open the Computer tab, then Map network drive.
mount.windows.3: Paste the address in the Folder box.
mount.windows.fix.title: If Windows can't connect
mount.windows.fix: The WebClient service opens these drives and is part of Windows. If the drive does not connect, start it as administrator.
mount.windows.fix.label: Start the WebClient service
mount.step.linux: GNOME Files or KDE Dolphin opens the files as a folder.
mount.linux.gnome.2: Paste the Linux address and press Enter.
mount.linux.kde.1: Open Dolphin and click the empty area right of the path.
mount.linux.kde.2: Paste the KDE address and press Enter.
mount.step.phone: iPhone, iPad and Android: the built-in Files app can't open this address. Use a WebDAV app.
mount.phone.1: Install a file manager app that opens WebDAV drives.
mount.phone.2: Add a WebDAV server in the app and paste the address.
mount.phone.3: Leave user name and password empty, unless a rule sets them.
mount.davfs.title: Without a desktop: davfs2
mount.davfs: Install davfs2 once (sudo apt install davfs2, or sudo dnf install davfs2). At the prompts press Enter, unless a password rule protects these files.
mount.davfs.label: Mount with davfs2
mount.key: The address is the key: anyone with it can open and change these files. You manage access in Keys and tokens.
